author: Frank Asante Van Laarhoven
question: once run_00001 entered its terminal region, did the frozen target-selection, terminal-approach or stopping semantics prevent or materially delay entry into the 0.20 m goal region before max_steps?
explicitly_not_asking: whether max_steps should be larger; Q1 settled that
whether the tracker caused the failure; that needs an intervention

skill_retrieval_preflight.error: CONNECT_TIMEOUT: MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms
skill_retrieval_preflight.diagnosis: unchanged from Q2 and independently reproduced: launched directly the server loads 89267 skills and then a SentenceTransformer embedding model onto CUDA with HuggingFace revalidation round trips, and was still initialising at 20 s. Cold-start latency exceeding the 30 s connect timeout, not an import or configuration failure
skill_retrieval_preflight.policy_reading: the global policy requires the search to be attempted and its outcome recorded, and provides explicitly for continuing on repository evidence. It sets no precondition that retrieval must succeed. Recorded, not bypassed

reconstruction_consistency_with_q2.method: the Q2-validated reconstruction, recomputed here independently

terminal_leg.PRIMARY_DEFINITION: the final planned leg: from the last interior route vertex to the sealed goal. Structural, taken from the frozen route, fixed before any behaviour was inspected

geometric_2m_goal_region.definition: first step within 2.0 m of the sealed goal

q2_turn_zone_offset_leg.definition: first step past the last interior vertex plus one G10 separator length, the Q2 phase boundary

terminal_leg.no_post_hoc_threshold: the primary window is the frozen route's own final leg. No distance threshold was chosen after inspecting the trace

target_selection.advance_rule_is_monotonic_by_constructio: the index only ever increments; regression is impossible in the frozen implementation, so observing none is a consistency check, not a finding

B_lookahead_target_advance.IMPORTANT: A and B are not two conditions. The same test both declares a vertex reached and advances the target, so a vertex that is never approached within the look-ahead radius is never passed

C_route_completion.effect: sets the `finished` property only. It is consulted at control.py:234 and ONLY when the body-frame target offset is under 1e-9 m, which did not occur. Route completion therefore never terminates an episode

D_navigation_goal_reached.CRITICAL: this is the FIRST statement in step(), evaluated BEFORE target selection. Its sole precondition is Euclidean distance to the final path point. It does not depend on the active target index, on the look-ahead radius, or on route completion

E_zero_terminal_velocity.predicate: fires if and only if D fires

other_exits.stalled: collect.py:598, stall_patience consecutive commanded steps with under 1e-3 m of motion
other_exits.collision_guard: collect.py:577, no step was refused in this run

event_order_per_step: 2. D: goal-distance test -> if true, stop with success
3. A/B: advance target index while within look-ahead of the current vertex
4. compute body-frame offset to the active vertex
terminal_predicate_contract.consequence_for_this_run: because D precedes and is independent of A/B, the stop branch could have fired at any step at which the base came within 0.20 m of the goal point, whatever the target index was. Target selection cannot have suppressed a stop that its own precondition never satisfied

stop_branch_reachability.reasoning: the stop branch's only precondition is Euclidean goal distance under 0.20 m. The closest the base ever came was 1.6787 m, 8.39 times the tolerance. The branch was never entitled to fire, so nothing about its behaviour can be assessed from this run and no stopping defect can be claimed or excluded on this evidence
stop_branch_reachability.not_a_defect_finding: a stop mechanism whose triggering precondition was never met is not thereby shown defective

terminal_progress.window_choice: thirds of the structurally defined terminal leg, plus quantiles. No last-N window was invented, because no frozen N exists

final_miss_decomposition.why_this_matters: route progress and goal distance are not interchangeable. A base that is off the path can advance along the route without closing on the goal, and at the end of this run that difference is most of the miss
final_miss_decomposition.reading: the final miss is almost exactly the right triangle of a 0.93 m shortfall along the route and a 1.40 m lateral offset from it. Even with the route run to its end the base would have been 1.40 m from the goal, still outside a 0.20 m tolerance. The dominant term is lateral

terminal_requirement.method: the terminal analogue of Q1, computed on two bases because they answer different questions and disagree here

route_progress_basis.question: did the base advance along the route fast enough?

goal_distance_basis.question: did the base actually close on the goal fast enough?

terminal_requirement.the_two_bases_disagree_because: cross-track error converts route progress into less goal closure. The base very nearly met the route-progress rate the budget demanded and fell well short on goal closure, and the gap between the two ratios is the lateral offset
terminal_requirement.classification_basis: insufficient on either basis is insufficient. Route progress missed by 1 percent and goal closure by 19 percent
terminal_requirement.interpretation: this compares achieved rates against what the remaining budget demanded. It does not license changing max_steps

target_rule_counterfactual.LABEL: COMMAND_FIELD_COUNTERFACTUAL_ONLY
target_rule_counterfactual.what_it_compares: at every recorded pre-command pose, the command the frozen control law would issue under two target-selection rules
target_rule_counterfactual.arm_1: the frozen implementation: the current path VERTEX
target_rule_counterfactual.arm_2: an arc-length interpolated point one look-ahead distance further along the polyline from the pose's own projection
target_rule_counterfactual.why_not: a command field does not determine a trajectory once the loop is closed. Q2 measured what open-loop integration does to a prediction here: it diverged to 0.229 m from a 2.3e-05 m seed

VALIDITY_DOMAIN_AND_BIAS.WARNING: this comparison is biased against the interpolated arm, and the direction of the raw result must not be read as a verdict
VALIDITY_DOMAIN_AND_BIAS.why: the counterfactual is evaluated at poses the CONTROL arm produced. An interpolated-target controller would never have visited them, so the treatment arm is scored off its own distribution
VALIDITY_DOMAIN_AND_BIAS.how_that_bites_here: the base ran far off the polyline. An arc-length point one look-ahead further along the path is then beside or behind the robot rather than ahead of it, which inflates the interpolated arm's heading error and collapses its commanded speed. That is a property of where the control arm went, not of the interpolated rule
VALIDITY_DOMAIN_AND_BIAS.classical_pure_pursuit_note: textbook pure pursuit takes the intersection of a circle of the look-ahead radius centred on the ROBOT with the path. With a 0.45 m radius and cross-track up to 2.589 m, no such intersection exists for most of this run, so that variant is not even defined here. This is itself a finding about look-ahead sizing relative to achieved tracking error

restricted_to_validity_domain.caveat: still evaluated at control-arm poses; restricting the domain removes the worst of the bias, not all of it

target_rule_counterfactual.RAW_RESULT_DIRECTION: on the terminal leg the interpolated arm shows a LARGER mean heading error and a LOWER commanded speed than the vertex arm. That is the opposite of the hypothesis that motivated this test, and it is reported unchanged. It is explained by the bias above rather than taken as evidence that vertex targeting is preferable, and it is precisely why the question needs an intervention rather than another offline pass
target_rule_counterfactual.CAN_ESTABLISH: how the command field differs at the poses actually visited
CANNOT_ESTABLISH: what trajectory the alternative rule would have produced
that the alternative rule would have reached the goal

distance_scaling.mechanism_from_the_law: wz = curvature * vx with curvature = 2 * lateral_offset / dist^2, so for a fixed lateral offset the commanded yaw rate falls with the square of the distance to the active target. This is algebra in the frozen law, not an empirical claim
distance_scaling.excluded: turn-in-place steps, where wz is set to max_w and not by curvature
distance_scaling.INTERPRETATION_LIMIT: these are associations across steps of one trajectory, in which target distance, heading error and route position all co-vary. They are reported as association. The 1/dist^2 relation is exact because it is the law itself, but that the relation DROVE the outcome is not established by a correlation

vertex_transition_discontinuity.observation: target distance and heading error change discontinuously at a switch because the target jumps between vertices rather than sliding along the path. The magnitude of each jump is tabulated above
vertex_transition_discontinuity.association_only: no intervention exists in this run, so a switch coinciding with a progress change is association. Nothing here is a cause

approach_versus_stop.reasoning: the base never entered the 0.20 m goal region, closest approach 1.6787 m. The stopping logic was therefore never entitled to declare success, and this run is not evidence about stopping behaviour in either direction
approach_versus_stop.consequence_for_SR_OSR_work: run_00001 must not be cited as evidence that the stop mechanism failed. It is an approach and execution failure. Evidence about the stopping problem requires an episode that enters the goal neighbourhood and then fails to terminate, which this is not

classification.decision_rule: the stop-trigger labels are decided by a predicate, not by a threshold: either the sole precondition of the stop branch was satisfied at some step or it was not. That test is prior to every approach label, because an approach label would attribute the failure to a mechanism whose entitlement to act was never established

secondary_contributors_within_the_approa.note: these describe where terminal progress went. They are secondary because Q3's primary finding is that the stop branch never became reachable, which is a statement about entitlement rather than about controller quality

labels_not_selected.Q3_STOP_TRIGGER_REACHED_BUT_FAILED: the predicate was satisfied at 0 of 1200 steps
labels_not_selected.Q3_APPROACH_TARGET_SELECTION_DOMINANT: target selection is implicated by the offline command-field comparison and by the 1/dist^2 algebra, but one observational run with no intervention cannot rank it against the speed law, with which it is confounded through the shared heading-error term
labels_not_selected.Q3_APPROACH_SPEED_LAW_DOMINANT: same confound, in the other direction. The speed law and the target rule both act through heading error to the active target and cannot be separated without varying one of them
labels_not_selected.Q3_NO_MATERIAL_TERMINAL_DEFECT: not selected: terminal progress ran below what the remaining budget required, so something material did happen in the terminal leg

classification.why_not_a_target_selection_verdict: the evidence is suggestive and is recorded in full, but target rule and speed law are confounded in this run. Separating them is exactly what the drafted one-factor intervention would do, and claiming the answer now would spend the intervention's conclusion before running it

q3_may_establish: which target was selected at each step
whether the goal and stop predicates were ever reached
that the frozen target law yields angular authority falling as 1/dist^2, which is algebra in the law
how an interpolated-target command field differs offline
q3_may_not_establish: that changing the look-ahead fixes the trajectory
that a controller modification improves success rate
that the physical robot would behave similarly
q3_authority_limits.standing_rule: the standing-instructions file, rule 9: causal order for a failed execution

next_experiment.name: TERMINAL_APPROACH_INTERVENTION_V1
justified_by: the stop branch was never reachable, so the failure is in the approach
terminal route-progress ran at 0.99 of the rate the remaining budget required
the goal vertex was never entered within the look-ahead radius, so the tracker steered at a single distant point for 444 steps
the offline command field differs materially between the two target rules at the poses actually visited

single_factor.arm_A_control: the frozen implementation, nearest qualifying route vertex
single_factor.arm_B_treatment: arc-length interpolated look-ahead point at the same frozen look-ahead distance along the polyline

held_constant: route geometry and the seeded generator
the collision guard and the kinematic drive
explicitly_forbidden: changing cruise_v or the speed law
changing more than one factor in the same run
next_experiment.primary_outcome: entry into the 0.20 m goal region before max_steps
secondary_outcomes: mean absolute heading error to target
next_experiment.power_note: one trajectory per arm establishes a difference in one instance, not a difference in expectation. A route population and a seed sweep are required before any success-rate claim, and that is a separate design
preconditions: a preregistration frozen before the first run

milestone_unaffected.run_00001: IMMUTABLE compatibility evidence; unchanged by Q3
